title: Coffered Ceiling and Box-Beam Strategy to Conceal Plumbing in a Second-Floor Renovation

locations.name: Second-floor project area (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript states 'Up here on the second floor' and discusses master bathroom and kitchen area within the same upper level; no explicit shooting-location data.

summary: This Old House frames a complex upstairs plumbing installation within a renovation, where traditional routing is blocked by steel beams. The crew leverages architectural coffers and box-beam chases to conceal pipe runs for a shower, tub, and toilet, routing drops down to the basement through vertical and horizontal coffers. They plan multiple coffers and even drillFloor joists to create additional chases, illustrating how ceiling design (coffer ceilings) can influence plumbing layouts in a tight, beam-conflicted space. The segment also touches on design credit for the coffers and wraps with a channel CTA.
